tyler (AE): heads-up — BrightGate is planning a POC to migrate off VendorX to redwood. they flagged 3 blockers: prompt parity, output deltas, and enterprise security paperwork. can se/eng jump in?
elaine (SE): on it. can we get a list of the top 20 prompt templates they use in prod? we should do a side-by-side diff.
tyler (AE): will ask them for the prompt set today. budget question: they want to know approx token delta risk for parity vs our gen costs — asked for a pricing delta estimate up front.
marta (Solutions): quick thought — run a small A/B test with their prompts through both endpoints and measure response divergence + tokens. i can script that.
chao (Eng): +1. also need to know which VendorX features they're using — e.g., stateful sessions, response-format hooks, streaming. some compatibility shims might be needed.
elaine (SE): for compatibility layer we usually map: request schema -> normalise prompt -> call model variant -> post-process to mimic vendor output quirks. do we want to expose a temporary shim in POC?
tyler (AE): they preferred minimal changes to client side. so a proxy shim would be ideal (transparent adapter).
chao (Eng): ok. i'll prototype a small proxy that rewrites vendor headers and normalises stop sequences. should be able to run in their staging env.
marta (Solutions): i'll put together the A/B harness. pseudocode for the harness: ```bash
# run both endpoints and save outputs
curl -s -X POST https://vendorx/api/generate -d @prompt.json > vendorx_out.json
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @prompt.json > redwood_out.json
# then compare tokens + response similarity
python compare_responses.py vendorx_out.json redwood_out.json
```
elaine (SE): perfect. add metrics: token_count, edit_distance, length_diff, and confidence heuristics.
tyler (AE): security ask — they said enterprise infosec needs our completed questionnaire + sample network diagram before legal signs off. sec-bot, can you drop the standard docs? @sec-bot
sec-bot: Uploaded: BrightGate_Sec_QA_2026.pdf to /shared/sales/brightgate/ (link: https://files.redwood/brightgate/bsg_sec_2026.pdf) :white_check_mark:
chao (Eng): for the POC we should list the known incompatibilities up front: tokenization differences, subtle decoding RNG variance, and any vendor-specific stop-token behavior. i'll draft a short doc.
marta (Solutions): timeline proposal: day 0-1 gather prompts + sec form; day 2-3 run A/B harness; day 4 analyze deltas and produce remediation plan (shims/transform rules); day 5 present results and next-step pricing.
elaine (SE): pricing note — if we need extra ingestion / reprocessing to match outputs (e.g., normalization passes), that will cost extra compute for the POC. estimate ballpark: +10-25% tokens during normalization run.
tyler (AE): client asked about fallback strategy if parity not achieved: can we auto-fallback to vendor-compatible variant or proxy to vendor temporarily?
hao (typo not in participants): 
chao (Eng): we can implement traffic-splitting and a fallback that routes certain routes back to VendorX while keeping metadata for billing. it's doable but needs legal review for dual-sourcing.
elaine (SE): action items: - tyler: collect prompt samples + feature list from BrightGate (due EOD) - marta: stand up A/B harness once prompts received - chao: prototype proxy shim + incompatibility doc - sec-bot: ensure sec questionnaire posted in shared folder
tyler (AE): i'll ping BrightGate and get the prompt payloads and their VendorX API contract. tagging this thread as the single source for sync. :seedling: any other blockers?
marta (Solutions): just to flag: if they use vendor fine-tuned models with special tokens, parity likely needs mapping rules. we'll surface that in the POC.
elaine (SE): noted. once we have sample responses we'll decide whether to pre/post-process or fine-tune a redwood-variant internally for better parity.
tyler (AE): thanks all. i'll update thread when prompts arrive. :thumbsup:
